chainSteps.label: Mechanism & pharmacology
chainSteps.reasoning: Mechanism signal strength: moderate (MSS 0.47). Potency profile (IPS 0.70): potency 0.55, selectivity 0.90, PK 0.90, engagement 0.40, therapeutic window 0.80. Translational reliability (TRS 0.52): target validation 0.35, indication fit 0.72, modality fit 0.80, translation rate 0.15. Uncertainty (σ² 0.27).

chainSteps.label: Animal model: murine tau pathology model — tau uptake/spread reduction + behavioral deficit protection
chainSteps.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm that in preclinical murine models, BMS-986446 (formerly PRX005) significantly reduced tau uptake and spread, reduced the development of tau pathology in vivo, protected against tau-related behavioral deficits, and co-localized with tau pathology in AD brain tissue — a coherent, multi-endpoint preclinical package. In vitro studies with the murine parent antibody 3D6 also demonstrated inhibition of neuronal tau uptake, reduced tau-induced neurotoxicity, and promoted phagocytic clearance. This is clearly positive and above-average preclinical evidence for an anti-tau mAb, supporting mu≈1.30 (above-average). However, tau mouse models are notoriously poor translators to human clinical benefit (the class has failed in human trials repeatedly: BIIB076, gosuranemab, semorinemab, zagotenemab all showed null Phase 2/3 results), and the published preclinical data for BMS-986446 remains at the summary/press-release level without a peer-reviewed in vivo dose-response study, so sigma2 is set at 0.28 to reflect moderate confidence in the preclinical signal itself — acknowledging both the reasonably complete endpoint coverage and the well-known translational gap in this target class.

chainSteps.label: Same-target anti-tau mAb analogs (gosuranemab, semorinemab, zagotenemab, tilavonemab, posdinemab/JNJ-63733657) — all Phase 2 failures; MTBR-specific sub-class (E2814, bepranemab/UCB0107) still in earlier development with no Phase 2 efficacy readout
chainSteps.reasoning: TIER 1 (same target — anti-tau antibodies in AD): Five documented Phase 2 failures exist. Gosuranemab (Biogen) failed its primary CDR-SB endpoint in mild AD (TANGO study) and also failed in PSP (PASSPORT); semorinemab (Roche/AC Immune) failed in prodromal-to-mild AD (TAURIEL) and mild-to-moderate AD (LAURIET); zagotenemab (Lilly) was abandoned after Phase 2 disappointment in 2021; tilavonemab (AbbVie) failed in PSP; and posdinemab/JNJ-63733657 (J&J) was discontinued from its Phase 2b AuTonomy trial in late 2025 — constituting a well-documented class graveyard (classFailures=5, classApprovals=0). TIER 2 (same modality — anti-tau mAb): No additional distinct programs beyond Tier 1. TIER 3 (same broad pathway — tau biology): Non-antibody tau approaches (OGA inhibitor LY3372689) also failed Phase 2. BMS-986446 targets the MTBR epitope (R1–R3), mechanistically distinct from the N-terminal epitopes of most failed antibodies; the MTBR-targeting rationale is shared with E2814 (Eisai) and bepranemab (UCB0107), but neither has Phase 2 efficacy data to constitute human POC for the sub-mechanism, so differentiatedSubMechanismWithPOC=false. The combination of 5 consistent, well-documented Phase 2 failures across multiple large sponsors with no approval yields strong negative evidence: mu=0.28 (well below average, reflecting class-graveyard signal) and sigma2=0.13 (low, because the body of negative evidence is large, consistent, and multi-sponsor, conferring high confidence in the negative direction).

chainSteps.label: Own clinical data: Phase 2 TargetTau-1 (NCT06268886) — ongoing, no efficacy readout yet
chainSteps.reasoning: The TargetTau-1 Phase 2 RCT (n=310) started enrollment in March 2024 and is not expected to reach primary completion until March 2027. Only safety and tolerability data ('safe and well tolerated') have been publicly disclosed; no tau PET, CDR-SB, biomarker, or any other efficacy readout has been reported. Because no clinical efficacy data exist, found is set to false and efficacySignal to not_measurable_yet. Default uninformative prior scores (mu=1.0, sigma2=0.60) are used, meaning this evidence category contributes no informative update to the model.

stages.name: BMS-986446 Phase 2 Proof-of-Concept (Double-Blind RCT)
stages.aiRationale: This Phase 2 RCT establishes proof-of-concept for BMS-986446 in early AD, testing whether the drug slows cognitive decline on ADAS-cog14 vs placebo over 52 weeks in amyloid-confirmed MCI/mild dementia.

trialDesign.endpointDescription: ADAS-cog14 (Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale–cognitive subscale 14-item) change from baseline at Week 52
trialDesign.enrollmentNote: 60 patients randomized 1:1 (placebo vs. BMS-986446), amyloid-confirmed early AD (CDR 0.5–1.0), double-blind placebo-controlled Phase 2 proof-of-concept

stages.endpointRationale: ADAS-cog14 change from baseline is the FDA-accepted cognitive endpoint in early AD proof-of-concept trials and serves as the gating readout to determine whether the drug shows meaningful slowing of cognitive decline vs placebo before committing to a larger Phase 3 program.
stages.comparatorSource: CLARITY-AD (lecanemab, NEJM 2023) + TRAILBLAZER-ALZ2 (donanemab, JAMA 2023): placebo CDR-SB decline ~1.5–2.0 pts/18mo → ~10% placebo responder rate; honest σ² for responder-threshold/cross-trial heterogeneity.

stages.name: BMS-986446 Phase 3 Pivotal Registration Study (Double-Blind RCT)
stages.aiRationale: Phase 3 expands to n=400 and extends treatment/observation to ~18 months to demonstrate robust, clinically meaningful slowing of cognitive decline vs placebo, providing the pivotal evidence for regulatory approval in early AD (MCI/mild dementia).

trialDesign.endpointDescription: ADAS-cog14 change from baseline at 18 months vs placebo control
trialDesign.enrollmentNote: n=400, randomized 1:1 double-blind placebo-controlled, CDR 0.5–1.0, amyloid-PET or CSF confirmed, ~18-month treatment/observation period

stages.endpointRationale: ADAS-cog14 change from baseline at 18 months is the expected primary registration endpoint for anti-amyloid monoclonal antibodies in early AD; this timeframe captures clinically meaningful slowing of cognitive decline and aligns with FDA precedent (aducanumab, lecanemab). Larger n and longer treatment duration provide robust evidence of disease-modifying benefit vs placebo.
stages.comparatorSource: CLARITY-AD (lecanemab, NEJM 2023) + TRAILBLAZER-ALZ2 (donanemab, JAMA 2023): placebo CDR-SB decline ~1.5–2.0 pts/18mo → ~10% placebo responder rate; honest σ² for responder-threshold/cross-trial heterogeneity.
